title: Causation vs. Correlation
coreMove: Demand a plausible mechanism or test before treating association as cause.
sourcePressure: Frozen support is thin. The safe core is the distinction between things moving together and one thing actually producing the other, with the chapter functioning as a practical warning against mistaking association for mechanism.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says correlation is worthless or that causal reasoning requires technical statistical tools.

sourceAnchors.name: Causation vs. Correlation
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen bundle confirms a supporting idea titled Causation vs. Correlation and gives only the narrow factual floor of association versus actual production
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The safe move is not to throw away the pattern; it is to ask what could actually make one thing produce the other.

hook: ice cream and drowning imported example
correlation is not causation slogan as whole lesson
examples: famous public-health example not in source

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a product manager tempted to claim that sleep-score nudges cause better work output
exampleSpecs.stakes: marketing may promise a cause when motivated users simply use the tracker more
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luke writes the possible third factor, already disciplined users, beside the rising sleep and productivity lines before approving the claim
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two rising lines glowing on a tablet in a dark bedroom

exampleSpecs.audience: a city mobility analyst reviewing a link between free helmets and fewer injuries
exampleSpecs.stakes: funds may shift away from intersection fixes if the causal story is wrong
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Eva asks whether safer riders are the ones taking helmets, then requests station-level crash data before claiming the helmets caused the drop
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a row of free helmets clipped to a bike-share kiosk

exampleSpecs.audience: a cafe owner seeing loyalty-card users buy more beans
exampleSpecs.stakes: a discount campaign may reward customers who were already loyal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent compares new loyalty-card customers with prior purchase history before saying the card caused higher bean sales
exampleSpecs.firstImage: warm coffee oil shining on a paper loyalty card

exampleSpecs.audience: a parks ecologist reviewing more bees after a planting program
exampleSpecs.stakes: the city may expand a program without checking weather and mowing changes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Adaeze lays rainfall, mowing schedule, and wildflower acreage beside bee counts before naming the program as the cause
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pollen dust on a bee-count clipboard

exampleSpecs.audience: a mobile app team seeing tutorial completions rise with retention
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may force a longer tutorial and reduce actual use
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tom asks whether committed users finish tutorials because they already intend to stay, then proposes a test that changes tutorial order for new users
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a funnel chart beside a phone stuck on step seven

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic administrator linking appointment reminders to lower no-shows
exampleSpecs.stakes: the clinic may overlook same-week scheduling changes that actually caused attendance to rise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Anya hold the reminder texts and schedule-shortening change apart until she can see which mechanism plausibly explains attendance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a reminder-text report under a stack of same-week appointment cards

skillTargets: ask for mechanism before causal claim
choose a practical test for a suspected cause

tryThisNowSpec: Find one pattern you are tempted to call causal. Write one mechanism that could produce it and one third factor that could also explain it.
